subject: Anthropology
title: Surveillance and Control
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Surveillance and Control.

hook.text: Your phone tracks you. Cameras watch the streets. Algorithms predict your behavior. The panopticon is now digital.

buildup.text: Foucault described how modern power works through surveillance and discipline, not just force and punishment.

discovery.text: People internalize the gaze. When you know you're watched, you regulate yourself. Power becomes invisible and automatic.

twist.text: Digital surveillance extends this to every domain. States and corporations now monitor behavior at unprecedented scale.

climax.text: Surveillance reveals modern power's nature: it doesn't need to punish. It just needs you to know you're being watched.

punchline.text: The most effective prison is the one you carry.

quiz.question: How does Foucault say modern power works?
options: Through surveillance that makes people regulate themselves
Power doesn't exist in modern societies

details.summary: Modern states use surveillance technologies — cameras, data collection, biometrics, and digital monitoring — to control populations. Foucault's concept of panopticism describes how the possibility of being watched causes people to govern their own behavior without direct coercion.
details.whyItMatters: Digital surveillance expands state power beyond anything previous regimes could imagine. Understanding how surveillance shapes behavior and political possibility is essential for evaluating the relationship between security and freedom.
takeaways: Modern states deploy extensive surveillance technologies
Foucault's panopticism describes self-regulation through potential observation
Digital surveillance expands state power to unprecedented levels

faq.question: What is Foucault's panopticism?
faq.answer: Based on Bentham's panopticon prison design, Foucault argued that modern power works not through visible coercion but through the possibility of being watched. People internalize surveillance and govern themselves.

faq.question: How does digital surveillance change political anthropology?
faq.answer: Digital technologies enable surveillance at unprecedented scale — facial recognition, social media monitoring, location tracking, and predictive algorithms. This creates new forms of state power, new modes of resistance, and new questions about privacy, consent, and political freedom.
